$comment: M70's password strength meter. Data, not code (CLAUDE.md), so the wording and the thresholds can be tuned without a build. `bands` are read in order and the first whose `minScore` is met wins. `common` is a short list of the passwords that turn up in every breach dump — it is not a dictionary and is not meant to be one; it exists so the meter can say something specific about the handful of passwords people actually pick.

advice.short: Longer is the single biggest improvement — aim for at least 12 characters.
advice.oneClass: Mix upper and lower case, digits and punctuation.
advice.twoClasses: Adding digits or punctuation would help.
advice.repeated: It repeats the same few characters, which is easy to guess.
advice.sequence: It contains a run like "abcd" or "1234", which is easy to guess.
advice.common: This is one of the most commonly used passwords there is.
advice.good: Long, varied and not an obvious choice.
